stages.UNIT_TESTS: sh -c 'out=$(cargo test --color never 2>&1); echo "$out"; echo "$out" | grep -qE "test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed" || { echo "no tests ran" >&2; exit 1; }'
stages.UNIT_TESTS_SELECTED: sh -c 'out=$(cargo test --color never 2>&1); echo "$out"; echo "$out" | grep -qE "test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed" || { echo "no tests ran" >&2; exit 1; }'

notes: `cargo test --lib` runs ONLY #[cfg(test)] modules inside src/. A crate whose tests live in
tests/ — the cargo convention, and what most real crates do — gets `running 0 tests` and
exit 0, so the gate reports green having executed nothing. Plain `cargo test` covers both.
cargo has no --passWithNoTests equivalent, so the zero-test guarantee has to be a guard in
the stage itself: grep the harness line for a non-zero pass count.
LINT is clippy. An earlier version of this file had it null to keep the fixture simple, and
because the scaffolder defers to this file, that simplification became a prescription — a
Rust project shipped with no lint stage at all. Fixture convenience is not a prescription.
SELECTED is the same command as UNIT_TESTS: cargo has no changed-files mode, and
compilation dominates the runtime anyway. The documented degrade-upward fallback.
The fixture deliberately uses the tests/ layout. An earlier fixture put its test inside
src/, and that convenient shape hid this exact defect from the harness built to catch it.
